Cell Phone Masts

By: Graham Coetzer | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
There's no denying that cellphones have vastly improved our lives, but as masts go up seemingly around every corner across the country, do we have any say in where?

Unique Selling Point:
We want to look at how various companies seem to be able to erect cellphone towers with complete impunity in suburbs across the country. There are multiple cases of residents lodging complaints but the building going ahead in anyway. Most of the towers seem to be built without proper public participation.

Summary:
There are two cases identified to look at: in Craighall Park and Lonehill. In Craighall Park, residents are taking the COJ and the company who erected the tower, Atlas Tower, to court. Only Atlas Tower is opposing the case. Atlas seems to be a relatively small company from the States, which has rapidly expanded in SA, putting up 135 towers in 2 years. They seem to target schools and churches, institutions who have property and can use the rental income. Our case studies are battling a tower put up on the grounds of Old Apostolic Church. The residents have in writing an agreement from the church with residents saying they would duck out of the deal with Atlas if residents objected. Residents even offered to pay the R4000 a month rental income. But the 30m tower has gone up in anyway. It turns out the church has a nation wide agreement with Atlas to lease their properties to the firm. It seems public participation in the construction meant nothing, despite most residents objecting and handing in their written submissions, no hearing or resolution took place. In Lonehill, MTN are putting up smaller sized towers(only about 15m). These aren't disguised as trees. Residents have been waging war against MTN for the past 18 months. Apparently the MO for major service providers is to approach resident's associations with incentives like installing fiber etc in return for exclusive use by the service provider. In essence, bypassing the full public participation process. The bigger story here is that cellphone service providers are using a tender put out by City Power for cellphone airspace in the city to bypass public participation. These smaller masts are erected on street light poles, and city power does not need public participation to put up street lamps. in the 5 square km's that Lonehill consists of there are 15 MTN towers.

Press Release:


Cell Masts
There’s no denying that cell phones have vastly improved our lives, but cellular masts are
mushrooming across suburbs with complete impunity. Several Johannesburg residents have
opted to pack up and sell rather than live next to a mast, often losing hundreds of thousands in
property value in the process. Carte Blanche asks: why are residents’ objections disregarded and
towers built with no public participation process?

Script:


Cellmasts
27 Sept 2017

Voice
We live in a techno centric world – and as our constant need to be connected to mobile devices and the Internet increases, so too does the need for infrastructure to support that connectivity. But as cellphone masts seem to go up around every corner, communities nationwide are voicing their disapproval.

Link Derek
This is why some homeowners in Craighall Park are in an uproar. A massive cellphone mast has been erected right next to residential properties, despite a long list of objections. And it’s happening around the country.

Sound Up Colleen Fandam
Colleen: I moved here 17 years ago, and I’ve been exceptionally happy here. It’s a lovely neighborhood, lots of young people with young children; it’s been a wonderful experience.

Derek: But now your house is all packed up?

Colleen: It is yes, and I’m moving.

Derek: Why?

Colleen: Because I’m decidedly unhappy about having to live next to the cellphone tower that the church has put up in their garden.

Voice
Physiotherapist Colleen Fandam lives right next door to the 30m high cellphone mast that’s been erected in Buckingham ave on the grounds of the Old Apostolic Church. The church earns a rental income from Atlas Tower, who installed the mast.

Sound Up Colleen
Derek: But Colleen it’s really just a large mast, by your wall?

Collen: It’s ugly, I think it devalues my property, and there are connotations to negative health effects that I am concerned about.

Voice
Bruce Bowden lives across the road from Colleen. He is one of the 90% of the residents asked for comment by the city, who objected to the tower’s construction.

Sound Up Bruce
Bruce: We had no response from the City of Joburg. All we heard next was a letter saying that it had been approved.

Voice
Estate agent Rebecca Staniforth says she has had first hand experience of the effects cellphone masts can have on property values in Craighall Park.

Sound Up Rebecca
One of the main reasons why I battled to sell it was because of this tower, and it was quite a distance away. But people still picked it up and mentioned that they felt it had health issues. But eventually I did sell the land. It was quite a substantial reduction in the price, by R400 000.

Voice
Carte Blanche has had a huge response on social media from viewers across the country with similar complaints. From Stellenbosch to Witbank, Durban North to Kathu, viewers have bemoaned cellphone masts going up in their suburbs, often without their consent.

Link Derek
In Lonehill residents are also waging war, but it’s a different story. They’re complaining about cellphone masts like this that have sprung up all over the suburb.

Voice
These are 4G towers, which allow users lightning fast wireless access to the internet. The City of Joburg, through their City Power division, are rolling out 1500 of these across the metropolis. They want anyone, anywhere to enjoy wireless access. But although these masts are disguised as streetlights and are built on municipal land, some Lonehill residents like Trevor Nel are fuming.

Sound Up Trevor Nel
Derek: Trevor why is the community so steamed up about these masts?

Trevor: You know Derek, people went off to work one day and they came back and these blooming ugly mast edifices were suddenly in front of their properties. No wonder people were angry. Here were their houses, they’d spent a fortune on them, and didn’t know what was going on in their communities.

Voice
Phillip Broentland has one of the 4G masts right outside his house.

Sound Up Phillip Broentland
So let’s put it this way. Without any warning, without any consultation, without any approach from anybody out there, they just dumped that thing in front of my house.


Voice
Phillip fears the tower will affect his health and property value.

Sound Up Phillip
I can tell you now that the value of my house has dropped by approximately 35 to 40 percent.

Voice
Another concerned resident, Nic Papas, says they were outraged to find out that the Lonehill Residents Association or LRA, a non profit organization run to benefit the community, had given their blessing for the 4G tower project.

Sound Up Nic Papas
Nic: The Lonehill Residents Association, by means of a letter, stated that the residents have approved for these 4G towers to be erected, when in fact that was not true.

Derek: So you dispute the powers of the LRA?

Nic: Absolutely. The LRA has no right to give the authority for a 4G tower to be erected in Lonehill unless proper public participation is done.

Voice
Former chairman of the LRA, John Siddall, says there was nothing sinister about their letter to Lonehill residents.

Sound Up John Siddall
It was part of a notification. As far as we were concerned that was a deal done by all the networks and City Power to say that what they would do was they would take out a lamppost or a street light and they would replace it with a pole. And they said would you please send this out and we said sure we’ll send this out.

Voice
So can you as a resident of your community object to the erection of a cellphone mast based on aesthetics, health concerns or property values? Both City of Joburg mayor Herman Mashaba and MMC for Development Planning Funzela Ngobeni weren’t available for interviews prior to broadcast. Sol Masolo from City Power says you can object, but the city doesn’t have to listen to you.

Sound Up Sol Masolo
Sol: The fact that we do public participation does not mean that… Public participation process is not a request for permission, it’s not-

Derek: Are you saying that you don’t need permission, is that what you are saying Sol?

Sol: We need communities to understand the value of this thing. It is important that the communities agree or accept them. However it is critical to know that as we do that, it is the job of the city to make sure that there is connectivity across the city. So that is the service that the city needs to give to the people of Johannesburg.

Voice
The City of Joburg is relying on the amended Electronic Communications Act to back its argument, saying the act does not make provision for public participation and it’s not a legal requirement. The also say they cannot refuse approval of a mast.

Sound Up Colleen
Derek: Just how angry are you?

Colleen: Angry enough to move. And to take them to court.

Voice
Fandam is one of the applicants in a case to set aside the City’s approval of the building plans for the mast in Craighall Park. The respondents are the City of Joburg, the Old Apostolic Church and Atlas Tower. Attorney Ben Schmullian, who will be representing Colleen, says his clients have a valid case.

Sound Up Ben Schmullian
There is a very powerful alternative remedy in the form of the Promotion of Administrative Justice Act.

Voice
The act was created to enforce section 33.1 of the constitution.

Sound Up Ben
…which says in essence, you are entitled to, as a citizen, lawful, reasonable and procedurally fair administrative action.

Voice
In a written response to Carte Blanche, the Old Apostolic Church say “the OAC strives to be a good neighbour and a good corporate citizen that abides by the rule of law in all the countries where it operates and will abide by the decision of the court”.

Sound Up Bruce
Instead of being neighbours that can talk about things, we have now reached the stage where we want to fight about things, which we wanted to avoid at all costs, now we’re fighting.

Voice
Atlas Towers declined an on camera interview, and in their written response to us said: “Atlas is opposing the application for review as it has rights as a tenant on the land owned by the Old Apostolic Church and has, after following the correct legal procedure, had its building plans in that regard approved by the City.”

Sound Up Sol
Derek: You know the point is Sol, you know where these cellphone masts are going up, why don’t you go and see the neighbors, don’t worry about people that you know are two avenues down the road, ask the guy who is right there?

Sol: No we have. We actually have asked the guy who-

Derek: We’ve got a number of residents who weren’t asked, and suddenly they’ve got this mast right above their house.

Sol: Ja we have consulted a lot of… and that’s why I’m saying it is the guy who comes out of the house and says guys I’m unhappy with this and that’s the guy we have spoken to.

Derek: Why didn’t you do it first and you wouldn’t have had all these problems and having to move the masts?

Sol: No, in any consultation you will have people who are happy and you will have those who are not happy. Like I said you will find a customer in the consultation process that will say I’m not happy with where the pole is. And we’ll look at it and say no but this is where the pole is supposed to be. So we’ll leave it there. But you will have another customer that makes appoint and you say this customer makes a point and you might move the pole, so it is how the consultation works.

Voice
So unless you’ve got the resources to fight a costly court battle, you’re at the mercy of the municipality.

Sound Up Nic
You can’t have a 4g tower outside a nursery school. You can’t have a 4g tower outside somebody’s bedroom on the second floor. You cannot do that, they haven’t conformed to any of the bylaws.

Voice
There is growing international concern about the possible health hazards of cellphone masts, but so far government is relying on guidelines by the World Health Organisation.

Sound Up Sol
And the Department of Health assured us that we are compliant with the electro magnetic fields, as dictated by the World Health Organization.

Voice
One thing is for certain: government is determined to bring South Africa up to speed in the mobile technology race, and until adequate legislation and policies are adopted to solve these kinds of disputes, the war for the suburbs seems set to continue.

Sound Up Nic Papas
We’ve been labeled as detractors, we’ve been labeled as trouble makers, we’ve been labeled as we’ve always got something against anything that they want to do in Lonehill. And we’re not going to stop until it’s done properly.
